title: Unit 1 Practice Test
note: Family practice for the Grade 6 Unit 1 Practice Test (Dividing Fractions · Multi-Digit Division · Decimal Operations). The blueprint is read from the real test paper, not inferred: 10 scored items across 6.NOS.1 (8 of 11 points), 6.NOS.2 and 6.NOS.3. The paper prints the older Common Core codes for those three. Fraction division dominates, and it is never asked as a bare quotient — the test wants a mixed number in simplest form (Q3, Q5), how many WHOLE units fit (Q4A), what the leftover means in the story (Q4B), and a tape diagram grouped into equal sections (Q6A, Q6B). Items rehearse those demands and each names the question it stands in for in `mirrorsQuestion`. Every item is copied verbatim from the authored Unit 1 lessons and tagged with `sourceLesson`; nothing is invented to fill a gap. The id follows the bridge-lesson shape the repo already uses (<numbers>-practice / <numbers>-review, pinned by tools/validate-lesson-catalogues.mjs) and stays off the numbered lesson spine, the same way 1-review and 6-1-6-2-practice do.
contentObjective: I can divide with fractions and mixed numbers and give the quotient as a mixed number in simplest form, say how many whole groups fit and what the leftover means, divide multi-digit whole numbers, and divide decimals in money problems.
languageObjective: I can name the dividend, the divisor and the quotient, and explain in words which method a problem needs and what my answer means in the situation.

vocabulary.definition: The total number being divided into equal groups (the number inside the division bracket).
vocabulary.definitionEs: El número total que se divide en grupos iguales (el número dentro de la galera de división).
vocabulary.visual: In 1,344 ÷ 12 = 112, the dividend is 1,344 — the total amount being divided
vocabulary.cloze: In 84 ÷ 7, the total amount 84 being divided is the ___.

examples.text: The 252 in 252 ÷ 6 (the total amount inside the bracket)
examples.why: It is the total amount being divided.
That is the divisor (the group size).

vocabulary.definition: The number of equal groups you are dividing into (the number outside the division bracket).
vocabulary.definitionEs: El número de grupos iguales en que divides (el número fuera de la galera de división).
vocabulary.visual: In 1,344 ÷ 12 = 112, the divisor is 12 — the number of equal groups
vocabulary.cloze: In 84 ÷ 7, the number 7 that you divide by is the ___.

examples.text: The 6 in 252 ÷ 6 (the number outside the bracket)
examples.why: It is the number of equal groups you divide into.

vocabulary.visual: In 156 ÷ 12 = 13, the quotient is 13 — there are 13 groups
vocabulary.cloze: The answer to a division problem is called the ___.

examples.why: It is the result of dividing.
That is the dividend you started with.

vocabulary.definition: What is left over when a number does not divide evenly.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Lo que sobra cuando un número no se divide de forma exacta.
vocabulary.visual: 17 ÷ 5 = 3 R 2 means 3 groups of 5 with 2 left over
vocabulary.cloze: When a number does not divide evenly, the amount left over is the ___.

examples.why: 20 divides evenly by 5, so there is no remainder.

vocabulary.definition: A fraction with 1 on top, like 1/4.
vocabulary.visual: 1/2, 1/3, 1/4, 1/5 — each represents one equal part of a whole
vocabulary.cloze: A fraction with a numerator of 1, like 1/5, is a ___.

vocabulary.definitionEs: Una fracción volteada de arriba abajo.
vocabulary.visual: The reciprocal of 2/3 is 3/2. To divide by 2/3, multiply by 3/2.
vocabulary.cloze: To divide by 1/2, I multiply by its ___, which is 2.

examples.why: That is the opposite, not the reciprocal.

vocabulary.definition: A whole number and a fraction written together, like 2 1/2. It must be rewritten as an improper fraction before dividing.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Un número entero y una fracción escritos juntos, como 2 1/2. Debe reescribirse como fracción impropia antes de dividir.
vocabulary.cloze: A whole number and a fraction written together is a ___ ___.

examples.why: A whole part and a fraction part.
Same value, but written as an improper fraction.

vocabulary.definition: A fraction whose numerator is greater than or equal to its denominator, like 5/2.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una fracción cuyo numerador es mayor o igual que su denominador, como 5/2.
vocabulary.cloze: A fraction whose numerator is at least its denominator is an ___ ___.

examples.why: The top is larger than the bottom.

vocabulary.definition: To write a fraction with smaller numbers that names the same amount, like 2/4 = 1/2.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Escribir una fracción con números más pequeños que nombra la misma cantidad, como 2/4 = 1/2.
vocabulary.cloze: Writing a fraction with smaller numbers that names the same amount, like 4/8 = 1/2, is to ___ it.

reviewWarmup.title: Warm-Up: The Four Kinds of Question on This Test

questions.explanation: 9 × 84 = 756. Running the cycle: 75 ÷ 9 → 8 with 3 left, then 36 ÷ 9 → 4 with 0 left, so the quotient is 84 and the remainder is 0.
choiceFeedback: 83 × 9 = 747, which leaves 9 left over — a remainder as big as the divisor means the quotient is too small. Raise the ones digit by one and multiply to check.
9 × 86 = 774, a little past 756. Nudge the ones digit down and multiply back to test it.
9 × 94 = 846, which overshoots 756. Recheck the tens digit by asking how many 9s fit into 75.
hints: Anchor on a fact you know: 9 × 80 = 720, which is close to 756 — so the quotient is just above 80.
Set it up as long division and DIVIDE first — how many 9s fit into 75?
DIVIDE: 75 ÷ 9 → 8. MULTIPLY: 8 × 9 = 72. SUBTRACT: 75 − 72 = 3. BRING DOWN the 6 to make 36, then repeat the cycle.
questions.explanationEs: 9 × 84 = 756. Con el ciclo: 75 ÷ 9 → 8 y sobran 3, luego 36 ÷ 9 → 4 y sobra 0, así que el cociente es 84 y el residuo es 0.
hintsEs: Apóyate en un dato que ya sabes: 9 × 80 = 720, cerca de 756, así que el cociente está apenas arriba de 80.
Escríbelo como división larga y DIVIDE primero: ¿cuántos 9 caben en 75?
DIVIDE: 75 ÷ 9 → 8. MULTIPLICA: 8 × 9 = 72. RESTA: 75 − 72 = 3. BAJA el 6 para formar 36 y repite el ciclo.

choiceFeedback: The decimal point went the wrong way. 0.7 fits into 8.4 many times, so the quotient is much larger than 1.
Check: 1.2 × 0.7 is only 0.84, not 8.4 — the answer is ten times too small. Multiply both numbers by 10 to get 84 ÷ 7, then divide.
You multiplied 8.4 by 10 but left 0.7 alone. Both numbers have to grow by the same factor for the quotient to stay the same.
hints: Ask yourself: how many groups of 0.7 fit inside 8.4? Since 0.7 is less than 1, expect MORE groups than 8.
Scale both numbers by 10 so you're dividing by a whole number instead of a decimal.
8.4 becomes 84 and 0.7 becomes 7. Solve 84 ÷ 7 — your 7s times-table facts will carry you there.
hintsEs: Pregúntate: ¿cuántos grupos de 0.7 caben en 8.4? Como 0.7 es menor que 1, espera MÁS de 8 grupos.
Escala ambos números por 10 para dividir entre un número entero en lugar de un decimal.
8.4 se vuelve 84 y 0.7 se vuelve 7. Resuelve 84 ÷ 7: la tabla del 7 te lleva directo.

questions.stem: A rope is 4 feet long. How many 1/2-foot pieces can be cut from it?
questions.explanation: Write 4 ÷ 1/2. Put a 1 under the 4, then Keep, Change, Flip: 4/1 × 2/1 = 8 pieces.
choiceFeedback: You did not flip the divisor. Put a 1 under the 4, flip 1/2 to 2/1, then multiply.
You divided 4 by 2. Dividing by 1/2 means flipping it: 4/1 × 2/1 = 8.
Dividing by 1/2 makes the answer bigger. Flipping 1/2 gives 2/1, a factor larger than 1.
hints: Note the numbers: the rope is 4 feet long, and every piece is 1/2 foot — smaller than a whole foot.
Start small: figure out how many 1/2-foot pieces fit into just 1 foot of rope.
Put a 1 under the 4 to get 4/1, then Keep, Change, Flip: 4/1 × 2/1.
questions.stemEs: Una cuerda mide 4 pies de largo. ¿Cuántas piezas de 1/2 pie se pueden cortar de ella?
questions.explanationEs: Escribe 4 ÷ 1/2. Pon un 1 debajo del 4 y luego Conserva, Cambia, Voltea: 4/1 × 2/1 = 8 piezas.
hintsEs: Fíjate en los números: la cuerda mide 4 pies y cada pieza mide 1/2 pie, menos que un pie entero.
Empieza en pequeño: averigua cuántas piezas de 1/2 pie caben en solo 1 pie de cuerda.
Pon un 1 debajo del 4 para obtener 4/1 y luego Conserva, Cambia, Voltea: 4/1 × 2/1.

choiceFeedback: That's multiplication or another operation. Division asks 'how many of this size fit in the whole.'
Does dividing by 1/3 make the quotient bigger or smaller than the dividend? Check your answer.
You have the dividend and divisor backward. Which is the whole, and which is the piece size?
hints: This asks how many 1/4-size pieces fit inside 1/2 — the pieces are smaller than the amount.
Keep, Change, Flip: keep 1/2, change ÷ to ×, and flip the divisor 1/4.
1/4 flips to 4/1, so multiply 1/2 × 4/1 across the tops and bottoms, then simplify your fraction.
questions.explanationEs: 1/2 ÷ 1/4 = 1/2 × 4/1 = 4/2 = 2. Dos pedazos de tamaño 1/4 caben en 1/2.
hintsEs: Esto pregunta cuántas piezas de tamaño 1/4 caben dentro de 1/2: las piezas son más pequeñas que la cantidad.
Conserva, Cambia, Invierte: conserva 1/2, cambia ÷ por × e invierte el divisor 1/4.
1/4 se invierte a 4/1, así que multiplica 1/2 × 4/1 arriba con arriba y abajo con abajo, y luego simplifica tu fracción.

reviewHighlights.title: What the Unit 1 test asks for
reviewHighlights.rule: Every question on this test is a division question, and most of them want more than a number. The numbers tell you which method to run — whole numbers use the long-division cycle, decimals move both decimal points first, and fractions get rewritten as multiplication — and then the question tells you what form the answer takes: a mixed number in simplest form, a count of whole groups, or an explanation of what is left over.
reviewHighlights.formula: a/b ÷ c/d = a/b × d/c  (Keep, Change, Flip)
steps: WHOLE NUMBERS (Lesson 2.6, questions 2 and 7): run the long-division cycle — divide, multiply, subtract, bring down — until the last digit is used. Write a placeholder 0 in the quotient any time a digit will not divide.

DECIMALS (Lesson 2.7, questions 1 and 8 — both about money): count the decimal places in the divisor, move that point to make it a whole number, then move the dividend's point the same number of places. Now divide as usual.

FRACTIONS (Lessons 6.1 and 6.2, questions 3 and 5, answered as a mixed number): write any whole number over 1 and any mixed number as one fraction, then Keep, Change, Flip. Finish the job — turn the improper fraction back into a mixed number and simplify it.

WHOLE GROUPS AND LEFTOVERS (Lesson 6.2, questions 4A and 4B): divide first, then read the answer. The whole-number part counts the complete groups; the fraction part is PART OF ONE MORE GROUP, so say what that part means in the story before you name an amount.

READING THE DIAGRAM (Lesson 6.1, questions 6A and 6B — a tape diagram): every section is one copy of the same small unit. Count how many sections make the whole amount, then group them by the number each item needs — the number of groups is the quotient.
reviewHighlights.watchOut: A common mistake in Divide Fractions is flipping the wrong fraction: students flip the dividend (the first fraction) instead of the divisor (the second fraction). For example, solving 3/4 ÷ 5/8 by flipping 3/4 to 4/3 and keeping 5/8 gives 4/3 × 5/8 = 20/24 = 5/6 — but only the divisor gets flipped. Keep 3/4, change ÷ to ×, and flip only the divisor 5/8 to its reciprocal 8/5: 3/4 × 8/5 = 24/20 = 6/5. Before you submit, check that the fraction you kept (the dividend) is still facing the same way it started.

level1.label: Run the long-division cycle. Fill in the quotient.
hints: Read the row left to right — it is one trip around the cycle: divide, multiply, subtract, bring down.
The Quotient column wants the WHOLE answer, not just the first digit. Keep repeating the cycle until no digits are left to bring down.
Row 1: after you bring down the 4 you are looking at 64. Divide, multiply and subtract once more, then read the digits you wrote across the top.
level1.explanation: Long division builds the quotient one digit at a time. In 384 ÷ 8 the first working number is 38: DIVIDE 38 ÷ 8 → 4, MULTIPLY 4 × 8 = 32, SUBTRACT 38 − 32 = 6, BRING DOWN the 4 to make 64, and 64 ÷ 8 → 8 with nothing left — so the quotient is 48. The second row runs the same cycle three times: 6 ÷ 6 → 1, then 7 ÷ 6 → 1 with 1 left, then 12 ÷ 6 → 2, giving 112.
level1.explanationEs: La división larga construye el cociente un dígito a la vez. En 384 ÷ 8 el primer número de trabajo es 38: DIVIDE 38 ÷ 8 → 4, MULTIPLICA 4 × 8 = 32, RESTA 38 − 32 = 6, BAJA el 4 para formar 64, y 64 ÷ 8 → 8 sin que sobre nada, así que el cociente es 48. La segunda fila repite el mismo ciclo tres veces: 6 ÷ 6 → 1, luego 7 ÷ 6 → 1 y sobra 1, luego 12 ÷ 6 → 2, dando 112.
level1.labelEs: Repite el ciclo de la división larga. Completa el cociente.
hintsEs: Lee la fila de izquierda a derecha: es una vuelta completa del ciclo divide, multiplica, resta, baja.
La columna Cociente pide la respuesta COMPLETA, no solo el primer dígito. Repite el ciclo hasta que no queden dígitos por bajar.
Fila 1: después de bajar el 4 estás mirando 64. Divide, multiplica y resta una vez más, y luego lee los dígitos que escribiste arriba.

level1.label: Rewrite each problem by making the divisor a whole number, then solve.
hints: The 'Multiply Both By' column is the key move: choose 10 or 100 based on how many decimal places the DIVISOR has.
One decimal place in the divisor means multiply both numbers by 10; then rewrite and divide whole numbers.
Row 1: 0.9 has one decimal place, so multiply 4.5 and 0.9 each by 10 and write the new whole-number problem in the row.
level1.explanation: Multiplying the dividend and the divisor by the same power of 10 slides both decimal points without changing the quotient. Each divisor here has one decimal place, so ×10 rewrites 4.5 ÷ 0.9 as 45 ÷ 9 = 5 and 3.6 ÷ 0.4 as 36 ÷ 4 = 9.
level1.explanationEs: Multiplicar el dividendo y el divisor por la misma potencia de 10 mueve los dos puntos decimales sin cambiar el cociente. Aquí cada divisor tiene un lugar decimal, así que ×10 reescribe 4.5 ÷ 0.9 como 45 ÷ 9 = 5 y 3.6 ÷ 0.4 como 36 ÷ 4 = 9.
level1.labelEs: Reescribe cada problema convirtiendo el divisor en un número entero y después resuelve.
hintsEs: La columna 'Multiplicar Ambos Por' es el movimiento clave: elige 10 o 100 según cuántos decimales tenga el DIVISOR.
Un decimal en el divisor significa multiplicar ambos números por 10; luego reescribe y divide números enteros.
Fila 1: 0.9 tiene un lugar decimal, así que multiplica 4.5 y 0.9 por 10 y escribe el nuevo problema de enteros en la fila.

level1.stem: Divide the whole number by the unit fraction: 5 ÷ 1/2.
level1.explanation: Put a 1 under the 5, then Keep, Change, Flip: 5/1 × 2/1 = 10.
choiceFeedback: That's what 5 × 1/2 gives — but this is division, not multiplication.
That flips the wrong number — the 1/2 flips, not the 5.
Too small. There are more than three 1/2-size pieces in 5.
hints: What is the whole amount, and how big is each piece?
Put a 1 under the 5 to make it a fraction, then flip the 1/2.
level1.stemEs: Divide el número entero entre la fracción unitaria: 5 ÷ 1/2.
level1.explanationEs: Pon un 1 debajo del 5 y luego Conserva, Cambia, Voltea: 5/1 × 2/1 = 10.
hintsEs: ¿Cuál es la cantidad total, y qué tan grande es cada pieza?
Pon un 1 debajo del 5 para convertirlo en fracción, y luego voltea el 1/2.

level1.stem: What is the first step in evaluating 2 1/2 ÷ 1/4?
choices: Divide 2 by 1/4 and ignore the half
level1.explanation: A mixed number cannot be flipped or multiplied as it stands, so rewrite it first: 2 1/2 = 5/2. Then Keep, Change, Flip gives 5/2 × 4/1 = 10.
choiceFeedback: A mixed number has no single numerator and denominator to flip.
Dropping the half changes the problem into a different one.
Division is not solved by adding the parts.
hints: Which number in this problem is a mixed number?
How many halves are in 2 1/2?
Rewrite it as one fraction before Keep, Change, Flip.
level1.stemEs: ¿Cuál es el primer paso para evaluar 2 1/2 ÷ 1/4?
level1.explanationEs: Un número mixto no se puede voltear ni multiplicar tal como está, así que primero reescríbelo: 2 1/2 = 5/2. Luego Mantén, Cambia, Voltea da 5/2 × 4/1 = 10.
hintsEs: ¿Cuál número de este problema es un número mixto?
¿Cuántos medios hay en 2 1/2?
Reescríbelo como una sola fracción antes de Mantén, Cambia, Voltea.

level1.explanation: Rewrite 1 1/2 as 3/2. Use the reciprocal of 1/4, which is 4/1: 3/2 × 4/1 = 12/2 = 6.
choiceFeedback: That multiplies without flipping the divisor: 3/2 × 1/4 = 3/8.
That is the step before simplifying — 12/2 still needs to be reduced to 6.
That divides the numerator and denominator by different numbers, which is not how this works.
hints: First, rewrite the mixed number as an improper fraction.
level1.explanationEs: Reescribe 1 1/2 como 3/2. Usa el recíproco de 1/4, que es 4/1: 3/2 × 4/1 = 12/2 = 6.
hintsEs: Primero, reescribe el número mixto como fracción impropia.
1 1/2 = 3/2. Luego voltea 1/4 a 4/1.

level1.instructions: Use the bar model to count how many 1/6-size pieces fit into 3 wholes. All 3 wholes are shown, each split into sixths.
level1.label: Model 3 ÷ 1/6 with a bar model — all 3 wholes are shown, each split into sixths
level1.totalLabel: 3 wholes split into sixths — count all the 1/6 pieces
level1.questionText: How many 1/6-size pieces fit into 3 wholes?
level1.hint: Count how many sections of size 1/6 fit into each whole on the bar. Then add them all up.
hints: Look at the bar: all 3 wholes are already split into 1/6-size sections, marked whole 1, whole 2, whole 3.
Count how many sixths fill just one whole first, then use that count for all three wholes.
One whole holds 6 sixths. Keep counting past 6 as you move through whole 2 and whole 3.
level1.explanation: The bar shows whole 1, whole 2 and whole 3 each cut into 6 sixths, so 6 + 6 + 6 = 18 pieces of size 1/6. The steps land on the same answer: put a 1 under the 3 and use Keep, Change, Flip, 3/1 × 6/1 = 18.
level1.explanationEs: La barra muestra el entero 1, el entero 2 y el entero 3 cortados en 6 sextos cada uno, así que 6 + 6 + 6 = 18 piezas de tamaño 1/6. Los pasos llegan a la misma respuesta: pon un 1 debajo del 3 y usa Conserva, Cambia, Voltea, 3/1 × 6/1 = 18.
hintsEs: Mira la barra: los 3 enteros ya están divididos en secciones de tamaño 1/6, marcadas entero 1, entero 2 y entero 3.
Cuenta primero cuántos sextos llenan un solo entero y luego usa ese conteo para los tres enteros.
Un entero contiene 6 sextos. Sigue contando más allá de 6 al pasar por el entero 2 y el entero 3.

level2.label: Complete each division problem.
hints: Every quotient can be checked by multiplying back: quotient × divisor should rebuild the original number exactly.
Run the long-division cycle on every row: divide, multiply, subtract, bring down, and repeat until the last digit is used.
For 672 ÷ 8: DIVIDE 67 ÷ 8 → 8, MULTIPLY 8 × 8 = 64, SUBTRACT 67 − 64 = 3, BRING DOWN the 2 to make 32, then repeat. Use the same cycle on every row.
level2.explanation: Each quotient comes from repeating divide, multiply, subtract, bring down until the last digit is used: 672 ÷ 8 = 84, 2,208 ÷ 16 = 138, 2,016 ÷ 14 = 144, 1,560 ÷ 15 = 104, and 3,276 ÷ 12 = 273. Multiplying back rebuilds each dividend exactly, so every row ends with a remainder of 0.
level2.explanationEs: Cada cociente sale de repetir divide, multiplica, resta y baja hasta usar el último dígito: 672 ÷ 8 = 84, 2,208 ÷ 16 = 138, 2,016 ÷ 14 = 144, 1,560 ÷ 15 = 104, y 3,276 ÷ 12 = 273. Al multiplicar de regreso se reconstruye cada dividendo exactamente, así que todas las filas terminan con residuo 0.
hintsEs: Todo cociente se puede comprobar multiplicando al revés: cociente × divisor debe reconstruir exactamente el número original.
Repite el ciclo de la división larga en cada fila: divide, multiplica, resta, baja, y sigue hasta usar el último dígito.
Para 672 ÷ 8: DIVIDE 67 ÷ 8 → 8, MULTIPLICA 8 × 8 = 64, RESTA 67 − 64 = 3, BAJA el 2 para formar 32 y repite. Usa el mismo ciclo en cada fila.

level2.stem: Table 1's lunch bill is $15.00. Every sandwich costs $3.75. How many sandwiches did Table 1 order?
level2.explanation: $15.00 ÷ $3.75. The divisor 3.75 has two decimal places, so multiply BOTH numbers by 100: 1500 ÷ 375 = 4. Table 1 ordered 4 sandwiches.
choiceFeedback: This divides the price by the bill instead of the bill by the price. Ask what is being split up: the $15.00 is being split into $3.75 pieces, so $15.00 goes first.
That is $15.00 − $3.75. 'How many' at a fixed price each is a division, not a subtraction.

The digits are right but the size is wrong. 40 sandwiches at $3.75 would cost $150, ten times the bill — that happens when the point moves in only one of the two numbers. Move it the same number of places in both.
level2.stemEs: La cuenta del almuerzo de la mesa 1 es de $15.00. Cada sándwich cuesta $3.75. ¿Cuántos sándwiches pidió la mesa 1?
level2.explanationEs: $15.00 ÷ $3.75. El divisor 3.75 tiene dos cifras decimales, así que multiplica LOS DOS números por 100: 1500 ÷ 375 = 4. La mesa 1 pidió 4 sándwiches.
hints: Every sandwich costs the same, so this asks how many $3.75s fit inside $15.00 — that is a division.
Set up 15.00 ÷ 3.75. The divisor 3.75 is not a whole number yet, so it has to be scaled first.
3.75 has two decimal places, so multiply both numbers by 100: 1500 ÷ 375. Now divide as whole numbers.
hintsEs: Cada sándwich cuesta lo mismo, así que la pregunta es cuántos $3.75 caben en $15.00 — eso es una división.
Plantea 15.00 ÷ 3.75. El divisor 3.75 todavía no es un número entero, así que hay que escalarlo primero.
3.75 tiene dos cifras decimales, así que multiplica los dos números por 100: 1500 ÷ 375. Ahora divide con números enteros.

level2.stem: Divide the whole number by the fraction: 8 ÷ 2/3.
level2.explanation: Put a 1 under the 8, then Keep, Change, Flip: 8/1 × 3/2 = 24/2 = 12.
choiceFeedback: That's what 8 × 2/3 gives — but this is division, not multiplication.
That divides 8 by 3/2 instead of flipping 2/3 first.
That divides 8 by 2 instead of by 2/3.
hints: Put the whole number over 1, then flip the fraction you're dividing by.
2/3 flipped is 3/2.
level2.stemEs: Divide el número entero entre la fracción: 8 ÷ 2/3.
level2.explanationEs: Pon un 1 debajo del 8 y luego Conserva, Cambia, Voltea: 8/1 × 3/2 = 24/2 = 12.
hintsEs: Pon el número entero sobre 1, y luego voltea la fracción entre la que divides.
2/3 volteado es 3/2.

level2.explanation: Rewrite 3 1/2 as 7/2. Use the reciprocal of 3/4, which is 4/3: 7/2 × 4/3 = 28/6 = 4 2/3.
choiceFeedback: That multiplies without flipping the divisor: 7/2 × 3/4 = 21/8 = 2 5/8.
That repeats the mixed number without doing any division at all.
That flips the wrong fraction before multiplying.
hints: First, rewrite the mixed number as an improper fraction.
7/2 × 4/3 = 28/6, which simplifies to 4 2/3.
level2.explanationEs: Reescribe 3 1/2 como 7/2. Usa el recíproco de 3/4, que es 4/3: 7/2 × 4/3 = 28/6 = 4 2/3.
hintsEs: Primero, reescribe el número mixto como fracción impropia.
3 1/2 = 7/2. Luego voltea 3/4 a 4/3.
7/2 × 4/3 = 28/6, que se simplifica a 4 2/3.

level2.label: Solve each decimal division problem.
hints: Every row uses the same move: shift both numbers until the divisor is whole, then divide as usual.
Count the divisor's decimal places to pick ×10 or ×100 — a divisor like 0.24 needs ×100 — then divide the new whole numbers.
Row 1: 9.6 ÷ 0.8 becomes 96 ÷ 8 after multiplying both by 10. Solve that, then apply the same shift to every other row.
level2.explanation: Once the divisor is shifted to a whole number, each row is ordinary division: 96 ÷ 8 = 12, 156 ÷ 13 = 12, 245 ÷ 35 = 7, and 576 ÷ 24 = 24 (that row needs ×100 because 0.24 has two decimal places). The last row becomes 113.4 ÷ 9 = 12.6, since only the divisor has to end up whole.
level2.explanationEs: Una vez que el divisor se convierte en entero, cada fila es una división común: 96 ÷ 8 = 12, 156 ÷ 13 = 12, 245 ÷ 35 = 7 y 576 ÷ 24 = 24 (esa fila necesita ×100 porque 0.24 tiene dos lugares decimales). La última fila queda como 113.4 ÷ 9 = 12.6, ya que solo el divisor tiene que quedar entero.
level2.labelEs: Resuelve cada problema de división de decimales.
hintsEs: Cada fila usa el mismo movimiento: mueve ambos números hasta que el divisor sea entero y luego divide normalmente.
Cuenta los decimales del divisor para elegir ×10 o ×100 — un divisor como 0.24 necesita ×100 — y luego divide los nuevos enteros.
Fila 1: 9.6 ÷ 0.8 se vuelve 96 ÷ 8 al multiplicar ambos por 10. Resuélvelo y aplica el mismo cambio en todas las demás filas.

level2.stem: A recipe needs 1 1/2 cups of flour per batch. How many full batches can be made from 6 cups of flour?
choiceFeedback: That divides in the wrong order — flip which number is the dividend and which is the divisor.
That's the reciprocal of the correct division, not the division itself.
That's the recipe's amount per batch, not the number of batches 6 cups makes.
level2.explanation: This is 6 ÷ 1 1/2. Rewrite 1 1/2 as 3/2, then Keep, Change, Flip: 6/1 × 2/3 = 12/3 = 4 batches.
hints: What is the total amount of flour, and how much does ONE batch use?
'How many batches fit' is a division question: total ÷ amount per batch.
Rewrite 1 1/2 as 3/2 first, then 6 ÷ 3/2 = 6/1 × 2/3.
level2.stemEs: Una receta necesita 1 1/2 tazas de harina por tanda. ¿Cuántas tandas completas se pueden hacer con 6 tazas de harina?
level2.explanationEs: Esto es 6 ÷ 1 1/2. Reescribe 1 1/2 como 3/2, y luego Conserva, Cambia, Voltea: 6/1 × 2/3 = 12/3 = 4 tandas.
hintsEs: ¿Cuál es la cantidad total de harina, y cuánto usa UNA tanda?
'Cuántas tandas caben' es una pregunta de división: total ÷ cantidad por tanda.
Reescribe 1 1/2 como 3/2 primero, y luego 6 ÷ 3/2 = 6/1 × 2/3.

level3.label: Solve each problem using long division. Show the quotient and any remainder.
hints: Each row asks for TWO things: the whole-number quotient AND whatever is left over — and a remainder can be 0.
Run the long-division cycle — divide, multiply, subtract, bring down — until no digits remain; the last leftover is the remainder.
For 2,578 ÷ 13: begin with 25 ÷ 13 → 1, subtract 13, bring down the 7. Keep cycling and record whatever remains at the very end.
level3.explanation: Long division keeps going until no digits are left to bring down, and whatever is still there is the remainder: 2,578 ÷ 13 gives 198 R 4, 3,456 ÷ 16 gives 216 R 0, and 1,987 ÷ 11 gives 180 R 7. You can check each row with divisor × quotient + remainder, since 13 × 198 + 4 = 2,578 and 11 × 180 + 7 = 1,987.
level3.explanationEs: La división larga continúa hasta que no queden dígitos por bajar, y lo que todavía esté ahí es el residuo: 2,578 ÷ 13 da 198 R 4, 3,456 ÷ 16 da 216 R 0 y 1,987 ÷ 11 da 180 R 7. Puedes comprobar cada fila con divisor × cociente + residuo, ya que 13 × 198 + 4 = 2,578 y 11 × 180 + 7 = 1,987.
level3.labelEs: Resuelve cada problema con división larga. Escribe el cociente y el residuo, si lo hay.
hintsEs: Cada fila pide DOS cosas: el cociente entero Y lo que sobra, y un residuo puede ser 0.
Repite el ciclo de la división larga — divide, multiplica, resta, baja — hasta que no queden dígitos; lo último que sobra es el residuo.
Para 2,578 ÷ 13: empieza con 25 ÷ 13 → 1, resta 13 y baja el 7. Sigue el ciclo y anota lo que quede al final.

level3.prompt: A recipe needs 2 1/2 cups of oats per batch. A baker has 8 3/4 cups of oats. How many FULL batches can be made, and how many cups of oats are left over?
level3.sentenceFrame: 8 3/4 ÷ 2 1/2 = ___, which means ___ full batches, with ___ cup(s) left over.
level3.hint: Divide first — the whole-number part of your answer is the full batches, and the fractional part tells you the leftover.
hints: Rewrite both mixed numbers as improper fractions, then use Keep, Change, Flip.
3 1/2 batches means 3 FULL batches, with half a batch worth of oats left — half of 2 1/2 cups is 1 1/4 cups.
level3.explanation: 35/4 ÷ 5/2 = 35/4 × 2/5 = 70/20 = 3 1/2. That's 3 full batches, with 1/2 of a batch left over. Since one batch uses 2 1/2 cups, half a batch is 1 1/4 cups left over.
level3.promptEs: Una receta necesita 2 1/2 tazas de avena por tanda. Un panadero tiene 8 3/4 tazas de avena. ¿Cuántas tandas COMPLETAS se pueden hacer, y cuántas tazas de avena sobran?
hintsEs: Reescribe ambos números mixtos como fracciones impropias, y luego usa Conserva, Cambia, Voltea.
3 1/2 tandas significa 3 tandas COMPLETAS, con media tanda de avena sobrante — la mitad de 2 1/2 tazas es 1 1/4 tazas.
level3.explanationEs: 35/4 ÷ 5/2 = 35/4 × 2/5 = 70/20 = 3 1/2. Eso son 3 tandas completas, con 1/2 tanda sobrante. Como una tanda usa 2 1/2 tazas, media tanda son 1 1/4 tazas sobrantes.

level3.stem: A robotics team is testing a new track design ahead of a regional competition. Their prototype track measures 5 1/4 feet from start to finish, and the competition rulebook requires the whole track to be built out of straight sections that are each exactly 3/4 foot long, with no leftover length allowed anywhere along the course. Before the team can submit their design for inspection, their captain needs to know exactly how many straight sections make up the full length of the track.
choiceFeedback: That's close to 5 1/4 ÷ 3/4 rounded down casually — redo the division with Keep, Change, Flip instead of estimating.
That's the track's total length, not the number of sections it's built from.
That multiplies 5 1/4 by 3/4 instead of dividing by it.
level3.explanation: Rewrite 5 1/4 as 21/4. This is 21/4 ÷ 3/4. Keep, Change, Flip: 21/4 × 4/3 = 84/12 = 7 sections.
hints: This is a mixed-number division problem — rewrite 5 1/4 as an improper fraction before dividing.
5 1/4 = 21/4. Now divide by the section length: 21/4 ÷ 3/4.
level3.stemEs: Un equipo de robótica está probando un nuevo diseño de pista antes de una competencia regional. Su pista de prueba mide 5 1/4 pies de principio a fin, y el reglamento de la competencia exige que toda la pista se construya con secciones rectas de exactamente 3/4 de pie cada una, sin que sobre longitud en ninguna parte del recorrido. Antes de que el equipo pueda entregar su diseño para inspección, su capitana necesita saber exactamente cuántas secciones rectas forman la longitud completa de la pista.
level3.explanationEs: Reescribe 5 1/4 como 21/4. Esto es 21/4 ÷ 3/4. Conserva, Cambia, Voltea: 21/4 × 4/3 = 84/12 = 7 secciones.
hintsEs: Este es un problema de división con números mixtos — reescribe 5 1/4 como fracción impropia antes de dividir.
5 1/4 = 21/4. Ahora divide entre la longitud de la sección: 21/4 ÷ 3/4.

level3.prompt: A gas station sells fuel at $3.45 per gallon. A customer pays $27.60 total. How many gallons did the customer buy? Set up the decimal division, show how to convert it to whole-number division, and solve.
level3.sentenceFrame: The equation is $27.60 ÷ $3.45 = ___. I multiply both by ___ to get ___ ÷ ___ = ___ gallons.
hints: Total money ÷ price per gallon = gallons, so set up 27.60 ÷ 3.45 — and notice the divisor has TWO decimal places.
Multiply both numbers by 100 so the divisor becomes a whole number, then divide the two new whole numbers.
27.60 × 100 = 2,760 and 3.45 × 100 = 345. Now ask how many 345s fit into 2,760 — note that 345 × 10 = 3,450 is already too big.
level3.explanation: Total cost divided by price per gallon gives the number of gallons, so the setup is 27.60 ÷ 3.45. The divisor has two decimal places, so multiplying both numbers by 100 gives 2,760 ÷ 345 = 8 gallons, and 8 × $3.45 = $27.60 confirms it.
level3.explanationEs: El costo total dividido entre el precio por galón da la cantidad de galones, así que el planteamiento es 27.60 ÷ 3.45. El divisor tiene dos lugares decimales, así que multiplicar los dos números por 100 da 2,760 ÷ 345 = 8 galones, y 8 × $3.45 = $27.60 lo confirma.
level3.promptEs: Una gasolinera vende combustible a $3.45 por galón. Un cliente paga $27.60 en total. ¿Cuántos galones compró? Plantea la división de decimales, muestra cómo convertirla en una división de números enteros y resuelve.
hintsEs: Dinero total ÷ precio por galón = galones, así que plantea 27.60 ÷ 3.45, y fíjate que el divisor tiene DOS decimales.
Multiplica ambos números por 100 para que el divisor sea entero y luego divide los dos números nuevos.
27.60 × 100 = 2,760 y 3.45 × 100 = 345. Ahora pregunta cuántos 345 caben en 2,760; nota que 345 × 10 = 3,450 ya es demasiado.

level3.stem: A board is 6 3/4 feet long. It is cut into pieces that are each 3/4 foot long, and then EVERY one of those pieces is cut in half again. How many final pieces are there?
choiceFeedback: That's the number of pieces after the FIRST cut only — don't forget the second cut in half.
That divides 6 3/4 ÷ 3/4 incorrectly. Rewrite 6 3/4 as an improper fraction first.
That's too few for a board this long cut into 3/4-foot pieces.
level3.explanation: First: 6 3/4 ÷ 3/4 = 27/4 × 4/3 = 108/12 = 9 pieces. Then every one of those 9 is cut in half: 9 × 2 = 18 final pieces.
hints: This is a two-step problem. Solve the FIRST cut completely before touching the second.
Rewrite 6 3/4 as an improper fraction (27/4) before using Keep, Change, Flip on 27/4 ÷ 3/4.
After finding how many 3/4-foot pieces there are, multiply that count by 2 for the second cut.
level3.stemEs: Un tablón mide 6 3/4 pies de largo. Se corta en piezas de 3/4 de pie cada una, y luego CADA una de esas piezas se corta a la mitad otra vez. ¿Cuántas piezas finales hay?
level3.explanationEs: Primero: 6 3/4 ÷ 3/4 = 27/4 × 4/3 = 108/12 = 9 piezas. Luego cada una de esas 9 se corta a la mitad: 9 × 2 = 18 piezas finales.
hintsEs: Este es un problema de dos pasos. Resuelve el PRIMER corte por completo antes de tocar el segundo.
Reescribe 6 3/4 como fracción impropia (27/4) antes de usar Conserva, Cambia, Voltea en 27/4 ÷ 3/4.
Después de hallar cuántas piezas de 3/4 de pie hay, multiplica ese conteo por 2 para el segundo corte.
